text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong makes personal pledge to Singaporeans in People's Action Party manifesto to work with them to make Singapore their best home.
- U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher arrives in Beijing for talks with Chinese counterpart Qian Qichen.
- Aztech Systems says may be liable for only 'modest notional royalty' in its copyright infringement battle with Creative Technology.
- Listed Malaysian marine engineering group Promet Berhad to make takeover offer for Ipco International.
- Indonesia President Suharto says individual shareholdings should not exceed 15 percent in companies on Indonesia's stock exchanges.
- Former United States embassy building on Hill Street expected to fetch Singapore $100 million.
- Thai stocks recovered by about 2.5 percent as investors more positive on composition of government coalition.
- National telephone firm Telekom Malaysia Bhd in joint bid with U.S.-based Southern Bell for billion-dollar privatisation deal of Telecom South Africa.
- Johor state government's new restrictions on foreign buying of residential and commercial property will not have significant impact on Singaporean buyers.
- Sound card king Creative Technology launches new sound cards.
- Thakral Corp reports 20 percent increase in interim after-tax profits to Singapore $28.67 million.
- Kuala Lumpur Promet Bhd offers U.S. $2.40 a share to buy another 29.6 percent stake in Ipco International.
- Small investors will get bulk of Ossia International's intitial public offer.
